checks_performed: Read only the authorized source JSON and draft JSON, plus the checker programs created in the authorized audit directory; did not use the web.
Independently compared the exact universal rational-DAG target with the scope asserted in the draft's final writeup.

Reconstructed the augmented-DAG path decomposition, grouped-path rounding, rational-certificate, conditional-expectation, Hoeffding, integral-flow, one-sink, normalized-integral-balance, and two-sink arguments.
Ran an exact Fraction-based exhaustive checker for the 3-by-3 grouped-incidence obstruction.
Ran an integer-only SSUF enumeration for n<=6, Q<=3 and n<=5, Q<=5 under the natural reconstruction of the draft's finite classes; no floating-point comparisons were used.

Checked for missing endpoint-balance cases, paths passing through other terminals, rational bit complexity, strict versus inclusive inequalities, and the assignment of the two integral unit paths to unequal sink demands.

claims.claim: Every rational input flow x has a polynomial-size rational source-to-sink path decomposition, whose total weight q_st for each ordered pair (s,t) satisfies q_st<=d_t<=d_max.
claims.evidence: Adding the supersource and supersink produces a conserved rational flow on an augmented DAG. Each positive source-to-sink path subtraction permanently zeros at least one augmented arc, so at most |A|+|S+|+|S-| paths are produced. Residual values retain polynomial rational encoding. The paths ending at t have total weight d_t, hence every nonnegative sub-total q_st is at most d_t<=d_max.
claims.search_method: Direct reconstruction of the augmented-flow decomposition and its arithmetic bit complexity.

claims.claim: After fixing the pair weights q_st, choosing one supported path P_st for every positive pair and assigning it weight q_st always produces a nonnegative unsplittable b-transshipment.
claims.evidence: Each chosen path contributes q_st only to the divergence at its two endpoints. The decomposition gives row sums b(s) and column sums d_t, so the selected paths have balance b. Nonnegativity is immediate, and exactly one path is used for each positive ordered pair. Sampling paths proportionally to their original weights also gives the asserted arcwise expectation used later.
claims.search_method: Endpoint-balance calculation for an arbitrary selection of one supported path per group.

claims.claim: On rational inputs, any real feasible unsplittable solution can be replaced by one with polynomially bounded rational encoding; consequently, existence is in NP.
claims.evidence: Fixing the at-most-one path for each ordered pair leaves at most |S+||S-| weight variables with rational row, column, nonnegativity, and arc-bound constraints. The feasible polytope is bounded because each weight is at most its source supply and sink demand. A rational basic feasible solution exists, and determinant bounds give polynomial bit length. Paths have at most |V|-1 arcs, so the paths and weights form a polynomial exact-arithmetic certificate.
claims.search_method: Rational-polytope and certificate-size proof using basic feasible solutions and determinant bounds.

claims.claim: The facts q_st<=d_max and E[Y]=x are insufficient by themselves for arbitrary grouped incidence vectors.
claims.evidence: The exact checker enumerated all nine row/column choices. Every fractional coordinate equals 2/3, while the selected row and column give value 2 at their intersection, so every outcome has maximum discrepancy 4/3>d_max=1.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive Fraction-arithmetic enumeration of all 3-by-3 row/column outcomes.
claims.witness: Two unit-weight groups: one uniformly chooses a complete row of a 3-by-3 coordinate array and the other uniformly chooses a complete column.

claims.claim: A dominant-path residual gives an exact, efficiently checkable sufficient condition for the target.
claims.evidence: For group i, arcs on which all supported paths agree incur zero change. On every other arc, consolidating onto a maximum-weight path changes the group's contribution by at most the total weight r_i outside that path, whether the selected path contains the arc or not. The triangle inequality gives |y_a-x_a|<=sum_{i:a in C_i}r_i. All sets, residuals, and comparisons are computable from the polynomial-size decomposition.
claims.search_method: Per-group two-case deviation analysis followed by an arcwise triangle inequality.

claims.claim: If every pair group has at most h supported paths and total supply B satisfies B<=h d_max/(h-1), the exact target holds; in particular, two-path groups suffice whenever B<=2d_max.
claims.evidence: For the meaningful integer range h>=2, a largest supported path has weight at least q_i/h, so r_i<=(h-1)q_i/h. Thus every dominant-path discrepancy is at most sum_i r_i<=(h-1)B/h<=d_max. Substitution h=2 gives the stated B<=2d_max case.
claims.search_method: Algebraic specialization of the verified dominant-path residual criterion.

claims.claim: There is a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm producing an unsplittable y with max_a |y_a-x_a|<=min(B,sqrt((|V|-1)d_max B)).
claims.evidence: For independent group choices, E[sum_a(Y_a-x_a)^2]=sum_{a,i}q_i^2p_ia(1-p_ia). Exact conditional expectation fixes one supported path per group without increasing this value. Since q_i<=d_max and each DAG path has at most |V|-1 arcs, the expectation is at most (|V|-1)d_max B. Maximum coordinate discrepancy is bounded by the Euclidean norm. Independently, both x_a and y_a lie in [0,B], giving the minimum with B. The conditional calculations involve polynomially many polynomial-size rationals.
claims.search_method: Variance calculation, exact conditional-expectation derandomization, and DAG path-length bound.

claims.claim: An expected-polynomial-time exact sampler improves the general relaxed bound to max_a |y_a-x_a|<=sqrt(d_max B ceil(log_2(4|A|))/2).
claims.evidence: For each arc, Hoeffding gives probability at most 2 exp(-2 lambda^2/sum_i q_i^2), and sum_i q_i^2<=d_max B. With L=ceil(log_2(4|A|)) and lambda^2=d_max B L/2, a union bound is at most 2|A|e^{-L}<=2|A|2^{-L}<=1/2. The squared acceptance inequalities are rational and exactly checkable. Rational discrete choices can be sampled exactly with expected polynomially many random bits, and the expected number of trials is at most two.
claims.search_method: Independent derivation of the Hoeffding constant, union bound, exact rejection predicate, and sampling complexity.

claims.claim: If the positive-support digraph of x has at most one directed path for every ordered source-sink pair, then y=x is already unsplittable.
claims.evidence: Every term of a path decomposition of x lies in the positive support. Path uniqueness forces all terms with the same endpoints to be the same directed path, so they can be merged without changing x. Capped path counting in topological order tests the condition in polynomial time.
claims.search_method: Merge argument applied to a source-to-sink decomposition, plus capped DAG path counting.

claims.claim: The exact target holds in polynomial time whenever there is only one sink.
claims.evidence: With one sink, total supply B equals d_max. Consolidating each source's decomposition terms onto one supported path preserves all balances and gives one path per ordered pair. Both old and new arc flows are between 0 and the total path weight B, hence their difference is at most B=d_max.
claims.search_method: Direct consolidation construction and total-flow range bound.

claims.claim: Integral lower-and-upper flow feasibility lemma: if an integral-balance flow g lies between integral arc bounds l and u, an integral flow z with the same balances and bounds exists and is computable in polynomial time.
claims.evidence: After subtracting l, the adjusted balances and capacities u-l are integral, and g-l proves feasibility. The standard supersource/supersink reduction gives an integral-capacity max-flow instance. Max-flow integrality supplies an integral feasible flow, and adding l back yields z with the original balances and bounds in polynomial time.
claims.search_method: Reconstruction of the lower-bound reduction to integral-capacity max flow.

claims.claim: The exact target holds whenever b(v)/d_max is an integer for every vertex; this includes all single-source instances with equal sink demands.
claims.evidence: For g=x/d_max, floor(g_a) and ceil(g_a) are integral bounds and all balances are integral, so the preceding lemma supplies integral z between them. Then y=d_max z differs from x by less than d_max on nonintegral arcs and zero on integral arcs. Each positive sink demand divided by d_max is an integer at most one, hence exactly one. A unit decomposition of the integral acyclic flow therefore has exactly one endpoint path per sink, precluding repeated ordered source-sink pairs. Equal-demand single-source instances meet the balance hypothesis.
claims.search_method: Integral rounding between floor and ceiling followed by a unit path decomposition.

claims.claim: For a single source and two sinks of scaled demands 1 and alpha<=1, there is a feasible integral two-unit flow z with lower bound 1 on H={a:x_a>1} and upper bound 1 on L={a:x_a<alpha}, with upper bound 2 elsewhere.
claims.evidence: Here 0<alpha<=1. Grouping a path decomposition by its two sinks gives f_1 and f_2 of values 1 and alpha. The flow g=f_1+f_2/alpha has integral balances +2,-1,-1. On H, g>=x>1. On L, g<=x/alpha<1. Each normalized component has total value one, so every g_a<=2. Thus g satisfies the stated integer bounds, and the verified integral-flow lemma supplies z.
claims.search_method: Arcwise verification of the fractional witness g for the integer lower/upper-bound system.

claims.claim: The exact target is computable in polynomial time for every single-source instance with at most two sinks, with arbitrary rational demands.
claims.evidence: The integral two-unit z decomposes into one unit path ending at each sink. Weight those paths by 1 and alpha. If z_a=0, the lower bound implies x_a<=1. If z_a=2, the upper bound implies x_a>=alpha, while x_a<=1+alpha, so the error from 1+alpha is at most one. If z_a=1, the new value is 1 or alpha, each within one of every x_a in [0,1+alpha]. Rescaling by the larger rational demand gives discrepancy at most d_max. All decomposition, bounded-flow, and scaling operations are polynomial-time exact operations; the one-sink case was separately verified.
claims.search_method: Complete z_a=0,1,2 case analysis, including assignment of unit paths to unequal sink demands.

claims.claim: No counterexample exists in the finite SSUF classes exhaustively checked by exhaust_ssuf.py.
claims.evidence: The independent integer-only reconstruction found no counterexample. For n<=6,Q<=3 it tested 4,653,917 deduplicated aggregate flows (4,393,587 after cross-resolution normalization); for n<=5,Q<=5 it tested 184,981 (169,568 normalized). These do not reproduce the draft's respective 4,146,045 and 168,336 counts. The authorized draft does not define the referenced script's graph-eligibility and distinct-flow conventions sufficiently to reconcile the counts, and the referenced script itself was unavailable under the read restriction. Thus the run materially supports but does not rigorously bind to the exact historical computational claim.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive integer enumeration of forward-DAG masks, reachable terminal sinks, all scaled-demand weak path compositions, and every one-path-per-sink output.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for a universal polynomial-time two-sided d_max result on every rational acyclic instance. The draft explicitly states that it proves neither that universal claim nor a counterexample. Its verified one-sink, normalized-integral-balance, and arbitrary two-sink theorems establish nonvacuous exact instances at the requested d_max strength, while the general deterministic and randomized results have larger bounds and do not close the target. The remaining cases include single-source instances with at least three nonuniform sink demands and general multi-source instances. Therefore the draft is VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS, not a full resolution. Its final writeup accurately disclaims universal coverage, and claimed_resolution=PARTIAL is ACCURATE. The unresolved finite-search provenance does not erase the independently verified proof-based special cases.
